newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: FIN MIN SAYS MULLS ANOTHER EUROBOND IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: FIN MIN SAYS MULLS ANOTHER EUROBOND IN 1997.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Tuesday that the government was mulling another eurobond issue before the end of the year.
"We are planning another (eurobond) issue, in German marks, by the end of the year," Shemeta said at a news conference.
"Of course, the issue will depend on concrete circumstances, but the amount should not be higher than the one set today," he added.

Lithuania on Tuesday set a $200 million, five-year eurobond at 105 baisis points over U.S. Treasury notes. It was Lithuania's second eurobond and the first public sovereign eurobond from the Baltic region.
Shemeta said that the conditions showed the international investor community had confidence in Lithuania.

"The low interest rate on this bond issue and the strong international investor demand puts Lithuania in the line of central European nations together with the Czech Republic, Poland and Slovenia," he said.
Sixteen investment banks participated in the issue which was lead managed by J.P. Morgan.
Shemeta said that 50 percent of the issue will be distributed in the U.S., 25 percent in Asia and 25 percent in Europe.

He said that part of the issue will be used to repay a $75 million syndicated loan which matures in September, part will be used to repay the country's debut $110 million eurobond, and the rest will be used to finance the budget deficit.
He added that the issue will also enable the government to reduce its domestic bowrrowing costs.
The country's foreign debt now stands at $1.4 billion while its domestic debt is around two billion litas.
